title: Solvent-exchange branch for blind material identity and process-history gating
scope: Additive hypothesis and metadata schema for comparing microwave-treated SCOBY residues with and without prior solvent exchange; not a validated synthesis protocol or experimental recipe.

new_process_branch.comparison_requirement: Any solvent-exchange condition must be compared against a matched non-solvent-exchange control before attributing differences to solvent exchange.
new_process_branch.hypothesis_boundary: Solvent exchange may alter dielectric heating, evaporation, shrinkage, thermal history and final residue chemistry, but the direction and magnitude of these effects are not admitted as established without measurement.

ethanol_branch.important_distinction: Ethanol substitution for water is a process-variable hypothesis, not evidence that the final residue is carbonized, porous or electrically conductive.
candidate_effects: changed capillary drying and shrinkage behavior
changed oxygen availability locally if vapor accumulates
possible changes in residual surface chemistry
not_admitted_claims: ethanol automatically creates a reducing atmosphere
ethanol-derived carbon deposition on cellulose is established under short uncontrolled microwave exposure

microwave_metadata.safety_gate: FLAMMABLE_SOLVENTS_MUST_NOT_BE_TREATED_AS_A_ROUTINE_MICROWAVE_INPUT; THIS RECORD DOES_NOT_AUTHORIZE MICROWAVE EXPOSURE OF ETHANOL OR OTHER FLAMMABLE SOLVENTS.
microwave_metadata.claim_rule: Nominal microwave settings do not establish sample temperature, local oxygen concentration, vapor composition or reaction pathway.

comparative_design_gate.interpretation_rule: No effect may be attributed specifically to solvent exchange unless the comparison isolates solvent history from precursor, mass, geometry, energy and atmosphere differences.

blind_identity_extensions.prohibited_inference: Appearance, brittleness, low density or black coloration alone cannot select among these material classes.

dielectric_heating.hypothesis: Replacing some water with ethanol changes microwave coupling and therefore the temporal/spatial heating profile.

vapor_and_pressure_behavior.hypothesis: A lower-boiling solvent changes evaporation and vapor-generation behavior during heating.
vapor_and_pressure_behavior.claim_boundary: The magnitude of pressure, mechanical disruption and pore preservation cannot be inferred from boiling point alone.

oxygen_environment.hypothesis: Accumulated solvent vapor can alter local gas composition, but does not by itself establish an inert or reducing atmosphere.

shrinkage_and_pore_retention.hypothesis: Solvent exchange can alter drying/shrinkage behavior because solvent properties differ from water.

surface_chemistry.hypothesis: Different thermal and solvent histories may alter oxygen-containing surface groups and other residue chemistry.

carbon_yield.hypothesis: Solvent exchange may change apparent and actual carbon mass yield relative to a water-rich control.
carbon_yield.claim_boundary: Higher carbon yield must not be assumed; retained solvent, mineral fraction, oxygen exposure and mass-loss pathways must be separated by mass balance.

ethanol_derived_carbon.hypothesis: Ethanol could contribute carbonaceous residues under some thermal conditions.
ethanol_derived_carbon.claim_boundary: No ethanol-derived carbon contribution may be claimed without appropriate isotopic, compositional or other discriminating evidence.

application_gate.rule: No supercapacitor, biochar, artistic-carbon or other application class may be assigned from the solvent-exchange hypothesis alone.
application_gate.electrochemical: Requires identity and structure gates plus normalized electrochemical testing and controls from v2.6.
application_gate.soil: Requires identity, leachables, pH, conductivity and controlled biological testing from v2.6.
application_gate.artistic: Requires identity, composition, particle characteristics and safety-relevant characterization from v2.6.

safety_boundary.flammable_solvent_microwave: Ethanol and other flammable solvents can generate flammable vapor and present ignition, fire and pressure hazards in microwave heating. This registry entry is an evidence-gating record, not authorization or instructions for microwave treatment of flammable solvents.
safety_boundary.sealed_system: Do not infer that solvent vapor makes a sealed system safe or inert; pressure and flammability hazards can increase.
safety_boundary.unknown_vapors: Thermal treatment of biological material and solvents can generate unknown vapors; characterization must be performed under appropriate laboratory controls.
safety_boundary.powder_handling: Unknown carbonaceous residues and fine powders require appropriate containment and inhalation controls.
safety_boundary.application_boundary: No human-consumption, food, cosmetic, medical or agricultural-use claim is admitted by this record.

decision_logic.gate_1: CONTROL_AND_RECORD_PROCESS_HISTORY -> thermal, microwave, atmosphere and solvent metadata.
decision_logic.gate_2: BLIND_MATERIAL_IDENTITY -> determine composition and transformation state while preserving competing hypotheses.
decision_logic.gate_3: STRUCTURE -> measure morphology, porosity, density and surface chemistry.
decision_logic.gate_4: FUNCTION -> only after identity and structure gates pass.
decision_logic.gate_6: APPLICATION_SPECIFIC_VALIDATION -> benchmark with explicit normalization and controls.
decision_logic.gate_7: CLAIM -> elevate claim level only when evidence crosses the relevant gate.

next_gate: REGISTER_A_MATCHED_SOLVENT-EXCHANGE_DATASET_WITHOUT_APPLICATION_EXPECTATION; COMPLETE PROCESS-HISTORY METADATA; PERFORM BLIND IDENTITY AND STRUCTURE CHARACTERIZATION; ONLY THEN EVALUATE WHETHER ANY FUNCTIONAL OR APPLICATION-SPECIFIC DIFFERENCE EXISTS.
authority_rule: This extension does not establish a solvent-assisted carbonization pathway. It only records testable hypotheses and strengthens the process-history and anti-confirmation-bias gates inherited from v2.6.
